anti_overlap: Covers data format and serialization; fd-go-python-subprocess-bridge covers transport; fd-mcp-tool-schema-discoverability covers MCP tool definitions
decision_lens: Does the QueryResult survive the full serialization path (Python dataclass → JSON → Go struct → MCP response → agent) without data loss or type confusion?
focus: QueryResult dataclass structure and serialization fidelity across Python to Go to MCP to agent
name: fd-queryresult-serialization-contract
persona: API contract specialist who has debugged serialization mismatches across language boundaries
review_areas: CanonicalID objects serialize to strings, not nested objects
entity_relationships returns actual entity data, not just relationship type names
datetime fields use consistent ISO format across Python and Go
Properties dict[str, Any] round-trips through JSON without losing types (int vs float vs string)
Nested structures (list of entities, each with properties) have bounded depth
Go-side struct tags match Python field names exactly

severity_examples.condition: CanonicalID dataclass not JSON-serializable, requires custom encoder
Agent gets ['imports', 'depends-on'] instead of actual source→target pairs
severity_examples.scenario: entity_relationships returns type names instead of edges

severity_examples.condition: dependency_count: 5 becomes 5.0 after round-trip, breaking Go integer assertions
severity_examples.scenario: Properties int values become floats in JSON

success_hints: QueryResult has a .to_dict() method producing clean JSON. Go-side has matching struct definitions. Round-trip tests exist.
task_context: The serialization contract spans three languages (Python → JSON → Go). Any mismatch silently corrupts data for every downstream consumer.
